newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T's Eagle Star hit by 91 mln stg charge.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T's Eagle Star hit by 91 mln stg charge.

text.p: B.A.T Industries UK insurance business Eagle Star has made a 91 million stg provision for U.S. asbestos and pollution claims taken in the nine months to September 30 and it remains unclear whether it will be sufficient, finance director David Allvey told analysts.

"We noticed an increase in the number of claims on U.S. pollution and asbestos so we increased the charge and the gross provision now stands at about 360 million," said Allvey at an analysts' meeting.
"Is it a one off surge through the summer? It is difficult to tell," he said.
The charge relates to business that has since been discontinued written through the London market.

Eagle Star's worldwide underwriting loss deteriorated to 108 million stg in the nine months to September 30, from 38 million stg last time. Eagle stars profit for the nine months was 32 million stg lower at 162 million.
In its general business, most markets remained very competitive, with little evidence of rates hardening. Worldwide gross premium income at 1.528 billion stg was down 12 percent.
In the UK, personal lines premium income was 23 percent lower, due partly to the loss of the Motability motor business.
In the life business, worldwide gross premium income (including unit trusts) rose strongly to 733 million, with overseas operations continuing to perform well.
Profit transfers from Eagle Star's life business rose five million stg in the nine month period up, from 25 million previously.
